title: A Qualitative Scoping Review of the Impact of Migration on Experiences of Intimate Partner Violence Among Latinas
abstract: Intimate partner violence (IPV) has several negative consequences in different life realms. Immigration can be a risk factor for women experiencing IPV, as survivors may lose protective factors such as access to protection services. This study aimed to conduct a scoping review of qualitative research to investigate post-migration barriers and challenges faced by Latin American immigrant women experiencing IPV. Qualitative papers were selected from 2019 to 2025 through Science Direct, Sage, Web of Science, Lilacs, Pubmed/Medline, SciELO, PePsic, and PsycINFO databases in English, Portuguese, and Spanish. We identified 23 studies, which revealed that structural and sociocultural hurdles, including a lack of documentation, fear of deportation, language barriers, and social isolation, mark the post-migration experience. Still, women demonstrate resilience and seek community support and specialized services, even in the most adverse conditions. Scholars and practitioners must develop intervention programs tailored to the migratory context of these women to guarantee their rights and promote their autonomy.
